readings.title: The Sabbath and the Passover
readings.subtitle: The Foundation of Holy Convocations
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘The appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which you are to proclaim as set-apart gatherings, <dn>My</dn> appointed times, are these:</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six days work is done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of rest, a set-apart gathering. You do no work, it is a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in all your dwellings.</dq> [4] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, set-apart gatherings which you are to proclaim at their appointed times.</dq> [5] <dq>‘In the first new moon, on the fourteenth day of the new moon, between the evenings, is the Pěsaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And on the fifteenth day of this new moon is the Festival of Matzot to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – seven days you eat unleavened bread.</dq> [7] <dq>‘On the first day you have a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the seventh day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Wave Sheaf Offering
readings.subtitle: The First-Fruits of the Harvest
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [10] <dq>Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and you shall say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, and shall reap <dn>את</dn> its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits of your harvest to the priest.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And he shall wave <dn>את</dn> the sheaf before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for your acceptance. On the morrow after the Sabbath the priest waves it.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And on that day when you wave the sheaf, you shall prepare a male lamb a year old, a perfect one, as an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [13] <dq>and its grain offering: two-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a sweet fragrance, and its drink offering: one-fourth of a hin of wine.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And you do not eat bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the same day that you have brought an offering to your <dn>Elohim</dn> – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq>

readings.title: The Festival of Weeks
readings.subtitle: Counting Fifty Days to Shavuot
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:15] <dq>‘And from the morrow after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought <dn>את</dn> the sheaf of the wave offering, you shall count for yourselves: seven completed Sabbaths.</dq> [16] <dq>‘Until the morrow after the seventh Sabbath you count fifty days, then you shall bring a new grain offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>‘Bring from your dwellings for a wave offering two loaves of bread, of two-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour they are, baked with leaven, first-fruits to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And besides the bread, you shall bring seven lambs a year old, perfect ones, and one young bull and two rams. They are an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And you shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old, as a slaughter of peace offerings.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And the priest shall wave <dn>את</dn> them, besides the bread of the first-fruits, as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, besides the two lambs. They are set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the priest.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And on this same day you shall proclaim a set-apart gathering for yourselves, you do no servile work on it – a law forever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And when you reap <dn>את</dn> the harvest of your land do not completely reap the corners of your field when you reap, and do not gather any gleaning from your harvest. Leave <dn>את</dn> them for the poor and for the stranger. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Memorial of Blowing Trumpets
readings.subtitle: A Day of Rest and Remembrance
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [24] <dq>Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘In the seventh new moon, on the first day of the new moon, you have a rest, a remembrance of Teru‛ah, a set-apart gathering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘You do no servile work, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq> ”

readings.title: The Day of Atonement
readings.subtitle: Afflicting the Soul on Yom Kippurim
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [27] <dq>“On the tenth day of this seventh new moon is Yom haKippurim.[a] It shall be a set-apart gathering for you. And you shall afflict your beings, and shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“And you do no work on that same day, for it is Yom Kippurim, to make atonement for you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>“For any being who is not afflicted on that same day, he shall be cut off from his people.</dq> [30] <dq>“And any being who does any work on that same day, <dn>את</dn> that being <dn>I</dn> shall destroy from the midst of his people.</dq> [31] <dq>“You do no work – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq> [32] <dq>‘It is a Sabbath of rest to you, and you shall afflict your beings. On the ninth day of the new moon at evening, from evening to evening, you observe your Sabbath.”</dq>

footnotes.a: Day of Atonement or Day of the Coverings.

readings.title: The Festival of Booths
readings.subtitle: Rejoicing in Sukkot for Seven Days
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [34] <dq>Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh new moon is the Festival of Sukkot for seven days to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [35] <dq>‘On the first day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [36] <dq>‘For seven days you bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. On the eighth day there shall be a set-apart gathering for you, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a closing festival, you do no servile work.</dq> [37] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you proclaim as set-apart gatherings, to bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, an ascending offering and a grain offering, a slaughtering and drink offerings, as commanded for every day –</dq> [38] <dq>besides the Sabbaths of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your voluntary offerings which you give to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh new moon, when you gather in the fruit of the land, celebrate <dn>את</dn> the festival of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day a rest.</dq> [40] <dq>‘And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of good trees, branches of palm trees, twigs of leafy trees, and willows of the stream, and shall rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for seven days.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And you shall celebrate <dn>את</dn> it as a festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days in the year – a law forever in your generations. Celebrate <dn>את</dn> it in the seventh new moon.</dq> [42] <dq>‘Dwell in booths for seven days; all who are native born in Yisra’ěl dwell in booths,</dq> [43] <dq>so that your generations know that <dn>I</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl dwell in booths when <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> them out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’</dq> ” [44] Thus did Mosheh speak of <dn>את</dn> the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Oil and the Showbread
readings.subtitle: Everlasting Covenants of the Set-Apart Place
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>"Command <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl that they bring to you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.</dq> [3] <dq>“Outside the veil of the Witness, in the Tent of Appointment, Aharon is to arrange <dn>את</dn> it from evening until morning before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually – a law forever throughout your generations.</dq> [4] <dq>“He is to arrange <dn>את</dn> the lamps on the clean gold lampstand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually.</dq> [5] <dq>“And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with <dn>את</dn> it, two-tenths of an ěphah in each cake.</dq> [6] <dq>“And you shall set <dn>את</dn> them in two rows, six in a row, on the clean table before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“And you shall put clear frankincense on each row, and it shall be on the bread as a remembrance portion, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“On every Sabbath he is to arrange it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually, from the children of Yisra’ěl – an everlasting covenant.</dq> [9] <dq>“And it shall be for Aharon and his sons, and they shall eat it in the set-apart place, because it is most set-apart to him from the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire – an everlasting law.”</dq>

readings.title: The Stoning of the Shelomith's Son
readings.subtitle: One Right-Ruling for the Stranger and Native
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:10] And the son of an Yisra’ěli woman, whose father was a Mitsrian man, went out among the children of Yisra’ěl. And the Yisra’ěli woman’s son and a man of Yisra’ěl strove in the camp. [11] And the Yisra’ěli woman’s son blasphemed <dn>את</dn> the Name, and cursed. So they brought him to Mosheh. Now his mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Diḇri, of the tribe of Dan. [12] And they put him under guard, that it might be declared to them at the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [14] <dq>“Bring <dn>את</dn> the one who has cursed outside the camp, and all those who heard him shall lay <dn>את</dn> their hands on his head, and all the congregation shall stone <dn>את</dn> him.</dq> [15] <dq>“And speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘Anyone who curses his <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bear his sin.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And he who blasphemes the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly be put to death, and all the congregation certainly stone him, the stranger as well as the native. When he blasphemes the Name, he is put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And a man who strikes the being of any man shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And he who strikes a beast repays it, body for body.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And when a man inflicts a blemish upon his neighbour, as he has done so it is done to him:</dq> [20] <dq>‘Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he inflicts a blemish upon him, so it is done to him.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And he who strikes a beast repays it, and he who strikes a man to death is put to death.</dq> [22] <dq>‘You are to have one right-ruling, for the stranger and for the native, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’</dq> ” [23] And Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ěl, and they brought <dn>את</dn> the one who cursed outside the camp, and stoned <dn>את</dn> him with stones. And the children of Yisra’ěl did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Seventh Year of Rest
readings.subtitle: A Sabbath for the Land
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh on Mount Sinai, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, then the land shall observe a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six years you sow your field, and six years you prune your vineyard, and gather in <dn>את</dn> its fruit,</dq> [4] <dq>but in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Do not sow your field and do not prune your vineyard.</dq> [5] <dq>‘Do not reap <dn>את</dn> what grows of its own of your harvest, and do not gather <dn>את</dn> the grapes of your unpruned vine, for it is a year of rest for the land.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the Sabbath of the land shall be to you for food, for you and your servant, and for your female servant and your hired servant, and for the stranger who sojourns with you,</dq> [7] <dq>and for your livestock and the beasts that are in your land. All its crops are for food.</dq>

readings.title: The Fiftieth Year of Release
readings.subtitle: Proclaiming Liberty Throughout the Land
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:8] <dq>‘And you shall count seven Sabbaths of years for yourself, seven times seven years. And the time of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.</dq> [9] <dq>‘You shall then sound a shophar-sound on the tenth day of the seventh new moon, on Yom haKippurim cause a shophar to sound through all your land.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall set <dn>את</dn> the fiftieth year apart, and proclaim release throughout all the land to all its inhabitants, it is a Yoḇel for you. And each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you return to his clan.</dq> [11] <dq>‘The fiftieth year is a Yoḇel to you. Do not sow, nor reap what grows of its own, nor gather from its unpruned vine.</dq> [12] <dq>‘It is a Yoḇel, it is set-apart to you. Eat from the field its crops.</dq> [13] <dq>‘In the Year of this Yoḇel let each one of you return to his possession.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when you sell whatever to your neighbour or buy from the hand of your neighbour, do not exploit one another.</dq> [15] <dq>‘According to the number of years after the Yoḇel you buy from your neighbour, and according to the number of years of crops he sells to you.</dq> [16] <dq>‘According to the greater number of years you increase its price, and according to the fewer number of years you diminish its price, because he sells to you according to the number of the years of the crops.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And do not oppress one another, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And you shall do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and shall do <dn>את</dn> them. And you shall dwell in the land in safety,</dq> [19] <dq>‘and the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat to satisfaction, and shall dwell there in safety.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And since you might say, “What do we eat in the seventh year, since we do not sow nor gather in our crops?”</dq> [21] <dq>‘Therefore <dn>I</dn> have commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth the crop for three years.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall sow <dn>את</dn> the eighth year, and eat of the old crop until the ninth year. Eat of the old until its crop comes in.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And the land is not to be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is <dn>Mine</dn>, for you are sojourners and settlers with <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Redeeming Property and Dwellings
readings.subtitle: The Rights of the Poor and the Levites
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:24] <dq>‘And provide for a redemption for the land, in all the land of your possession.</dq> [25] <dq>‘When your brother becomes poor, and has sold some of his possession, and his redeemer, a close relative comes to redeem it, then he shall redeem what his brother sold.</dq> [26] <dq>‘And when the man has no one to redeem it, but he himself becomes able to redeem it,</dq> [27] <dq>then let him count the years since its sale, and return the remainder to the man to whom he sold it, that he shall return to his possession.</dq> [28] <dq>‘And if his hand has not found enough to give back to him, then what was sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the Year of Yoḇel. And it shall be released in the Yoḇel, and he shall return to his possession.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And when a man sells a house in a walled city, then his right of redemption shall be at the end of the year after it is sold. His right of redemption lasts a year.</dq> [30] <dq>‘But if it is not redeemed within a complete year, then the house in the walled city shall be established beyond reclaim to the buyer of it, throughout his generations. It is not released in the Yoḇel.</dq> [31] <dq>‘The houses of villages, however, which have no wall around them are reckoned as the field of the country. A right of redemption belongs to it, and they are released in the Yoḇel.</dq> [32] <dq>‘As for the cities of the Lěvites, and the houses in the cities of their possession, the Lěvites have a right of redemption forever.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And that which is redeemed from the Lěvites, both the sale of a house and the city of his possession shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, because the houses in the cities of the Lěvites are their possession in the midst of the children of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [34] <dq>‘But the field of the open land of their cities is not sold, for it is their everlasting possession.</dq>

readings.title: Compassion for the Poor and Servants
readings.subtitle: Fearing Elohim in Lending and Labor
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:35] <dq>‘And when your brother becomes poor, and his hand has failed with you, then you shall strengthen him, and he shall live with you, like a stranger or a sojourner.</dq> [36] <dq>‘Take no interest from him, or profit, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and your brother shall live with you.</dq> [37] <dq>‘Do not lend him your silver on interest, and do not lend him your food for profit.</dq> [38] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought <dn>את</dn> you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you <dn>את</dn> the land of Kena‛an, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And when your brother who dwells by you becomes poor, and sells himself to you, do not make him serve as a slave.</dq> [40] <dq>‘But as a hired servant, as a settler he is with you, and serves you until the Year of Yoḇel.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And then he shall leave you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own clan, even return to the possession of his fathers.</dq> [42] <dq>‘For they are <dn>My</dn> servants, whom <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> out of the land of Mitsrayim, they are not sold as slaves.</dq> [43] <dq>‘Do not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [44] <dq>‘And your male and female slaves whom you have from the nations that are around you, from them you buy male and female slaves,</dq> [45] <dq>and also from the sons of the strangers sojourning among you, from them you buy, and from their clans who are with you, which they shall bring forth in your land, and they shall be your property.</dq> [46] <dq>‘And you shall take <dn>את</dn> them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them as a possession, they are your slaves for all time. But over your brothers, the children of Yisra’ěl, you do not rule with harshness, one over another.</dq> [47] <dq>‘Now when a sojourner or a settler with you becomes rich, and your brother with him becomes poor, and sells himself to the settler or sojourner with you, or to a member of the sojourner’s clan,</dq> [48] <dq>after he has been sold, there is a right of redemption to him – one of his brothers does redeem him,</dq> [49] <dq>or his uncle or his uncle’s son does redeem him, or anyone who is a close relative to him in his clan does redeem him, or if he is able, then he shall redeem himself.</dq> [50] <dq>‘And he shall reckon with him who bought him: The price of his release shall be according to the number of years, from the year that he was sold to him until the Year of Yoḇel; as the days of a hired servant it is with him.</dq> [51] <dq>‘If there are yet many years, according to them he repays the price of his redemption, from the silver of his purchase.</dq> [52] <dq>‘And if few years are left until the Year of Yoḇel, then he shall reckon with him, and according to his years he repays him the price of his redemption.</dq> [53] <dq>‘He is with him as a yearly hired servant, and he does not rule with harshness over him before your eyes.</dq> [54] <dq>‘And if he is not redeemed in these years, then he shall be released in the Year of Yoḇel, he and his children with him.</dq> [55] <dq>‘Because the children of Yisra’ěl are servants to <dn>Me</dn>, they are <dn>My</dn> servants whom <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
